title: A poppy seed with plans
body: Your baby is the size of a poppy seed and the neural tube is already forming — this is folic acid's big moment, so keep that prenatal going.

title: A heartbeat begins
body: About the size of a lentil, with a tiny heart starting to beat. If nausea has arrived, ginger and vitamin B6 are the gentle first-line helpers.

title: Raspberry milestone
body: Fingers and toes are budding. Fatigue is real right now — check labels on energy drinks; caffeine counts add up faster than you'd think.

title: Officially a fetus
body: The most sensitive window of organ development is wrapping up. It's a good week to double-check your skincare shelf for retinoids.

title: The strawberry stage
body: Reflexes are kicking in — literally. Many parents share their news soon; many also breathe easier as the first trimester closes.

title: Welcome to T2
body: The honeymoon trimester. Appetite often returns — a great time to get low-mercury fish like salmon on the menu for brain-building DHA.

title: An avocado, listening
body: Ears are formed enough to catch muffled sounds. Your voice is already the favorite. Keep the water bottle close — plasma volume is surging.

title: First flutters
body: Somewhere between gas bubble and butterfly — those first movements are showing up. Sunscreen matters more now too: pregnancy skin pigments easily.

title: Halfway there
body: The anatomy-scan week for many. Baby is about a banana long and practicing swallowing — everything you eat is flavoring the amniotic fluid.

title: A papaya with eyebrows
body: Eyebrows, eyelids and even fingerprints are in. If heartburn is creeping in, famotidine is generally considered a safe ask for your provider.

title: Viability week
body: Lungs are making surfactant and hearing is sharp. The glucose screen is coming up — one sweet drink where the sugar is genuinely for science.

title: Eyes opening
body: Baby's eyes open this week and breathing practice begins. Iron needs peak around now — pair iron-rich meals with vitamin C to absorb more of it.

title: Hello, third trimester
body: Welcome to T3 — and a safety shift: NSAIDs like ibuprofen are now off the table, so acetaminophen becomes the go-to for aches.

title: A cabbage doing squats
body: Baby is putting on fat and practicing big stretches. Sleep gets creative from here — a pillow between the knees earns its keep.

title: Head-down, hopefully
body: Many babies flip head-down around now. Braxton Hicks warm-ups are normal; regular, strengthening contractions are the ones to call about.

title: The final polish
body: Lungs and brain are in their finishing sprint. If you're prepping the hospital bag, toss in your own toiletries — you know what's on their labels.

title: Almost full-term
body: Baby is the size of romaine and dropping lower. Weekly check-ins usually start now — bring your medication questions, all of them.

title: Full-term and ready
body: Officially full-term. Baby is mostly gaining weight and growing hair. Keep meals light and iron-rich; your body is stocking up for the big day.

title: Any day now
body: Due dates are estimates — only about 5% of babies actually use them. Rest, hydrate, and keep your provider's number close. You've got this.
